agency.name: Център за градска мобилност (Sofia Urban Mobility Center)
agency.operating_note: Bulgaria's first reviewed feed record. Sofia city transport published by the municipal Urban Mobility Center on Sofia's open data portal.

findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 4454 of 4454 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 31965 of 31965 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the transit vehicle itself can take them.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Rename stops to mixed case where the language has letter case (for example, 'Central Station').
findings.what: About 3999 stop names are written in ALL CAPS.
findings.why: Mixed-case names are easier to read in apps and are read more naturally by screen readers.

findings.what: This feed describes station pathways, including step-free (elevator) routes.
findings.why: Riders can be routed through the station, and wheelchair users can see whether a step-free route exists.

completeness.name: completeness
completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is published.

findings.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
findings.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
findings.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.

findings.fix: Turn on 'remove unused shapes' (or the like) in your export tool.
findings.what: The feed contains route shapes no trip uses.
findings.why: Harmless to riders, but it bloats the feed and suggests stale export data.

findings.effort: A review pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove retired stops from the export, or add them back to the trips that should serve them.
findings.what: Some stops exist in the feed but no trip ever stops at them.
findings.why: Riders may walk to a stop where no transit vehicle is scheduled to arrive.

findings.fix: Review the rule documentation for 'unsorted_stop_times' at https://gtfs-validator.mobilitydata.org/rules.html and check the flagged rows in your feed.
findings.what: Unsorted stop times (flagged by the MobilityData validator).
findings.why: See the linked rule for what this affects.

findings.effort: Two fields in feed_info.txt, or one export setting.
findings.fix: Widen feed_start_date and feed_end_date to cover all service dates, or fix the dates that fall outside.
findings.what: Some service dates fall outside the date window set in feed_info.txt.
findings.why: feed_info.txt should span every day your service runs, so apps know when the data applies.

findings.effort: Usually a bulk edit in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Set trip_headsign to the trip's last stop or its overall destination.
findings.what: Some trip headsigns name a stop along the way, not the final destination.
findings.why: The sign should tell riders where the transit vehicle ends up, so a midpoint name can send them the wrong way.

correctness.name: correctness
correctness.summary: The MobilityData validator flagged 6 kinds of issue across 37771 instances (0 error, 30391 warning, 7380 informational).

freshness.name: freshness
freshness.summary: Service data covers the next 365 days.

findings.effort: A habit in your alerts tool, not a code change.
findings.fix: Give every alert a one-line plain-language header in your alerts tool; the description field can carry the detail.
findings.what: 17 of 17 published service alerts have no header text.
findings.why: An alert without text shows riders an empty or generic notice, so the disruption it describes goes unread.

findings.fix: Check with your AVL vendor that every vehicle assignment flows into TripUpdates, including school-day and tripper runs.
findings.what: 37 of 539 trips scheduled during the sampling window had no live predictions.
findings.why: Riders on those trips get schedule data dressed up as realtime. Caltrans expects every operating trip in TripUpdates.

realtime.name: realtime
realtime.summary: Sampled 9 times: 3 of 3 configured feeds healthy; 93.1% of scheduled trips had live predictions; 100.0% of vehicles on their route; predictions ran a median of 0s behind schedule.

notes: All four score categories were measured this run.
Realtime was sampled in one bounded window of 9 snapshots.
The feed was downloaded from the agency's own URL.

criteria.detail: Service data covers the next 365 days.
States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 0% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

conformance.summary: This feed is close to the conformance mark. States wheelchair access on 0% of stops and 0% of trips; the mark needs 90% of each.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 56 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (M1, 6, 7, 13, 6TM, and more).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 4 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("МИЗИЯ / НБУ", "Ж.К. МЛАДОСТ-1/БЛ. 70/", "Ж.К. МЛАДОСТ-1/БЛ. 70/", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.

findings.effort: A cleanup pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove stops no route serves, or add the trips that should call at them.
findings.what: 1135 of 4388 boardable stops are never served by any trip.
findings.why: Riders see these stops in apps and on the map but can never catch anything there, which erodes trust in the data.

scoring_profile.provenance: GTFS Scorecard's project-authored weights, deductions, thresholds, grade bands, and fix ranking, informed by the California Transit Data Guidelines and the MobilityData gtfs-validator. It is not a worldwide standard or a compliance determination.

top_fixes.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
top_fixes.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
top_fixes.what: 4454 of 4454 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
top_fixes.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

top_fixes.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
top_fixes.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
top_fixes.what: 31965 of 31965 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
top_fixes.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the transit vehicle itself can take them.

top_fixes.effort: Often a bulk fix in your scheduling software.
top_fixes.fix: Use mixed case for stop names and headsigns (e.g. 'Main St & 2nd Ave', not 'MAIN ST & 2ND AVE').
top_fixes.what: Some rider-facing names are in ALL CAPS or all lowercase.
top_fixes.why: ALL-CAPS stop and headsign names are harder to read in apps and are read awkwardly by screen readers.
